title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with current organizer instructions and the visible dated agenda; only 14–16 October entries were visible in the 11 October listing read. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates between Qawra and the Ta’ Qali event area, not confirmed hotel-to-gate journeys. An Eventbrite listing read 11 October gives the venue address and coordinates and publishes agenda times for 14–16 October; the traveler’s own reservation, gate, 17–18 October agenda and exact route remain unconfirmed. MPT’s fare table lists seasonal single prices (€2.50 summer / €2.00 winter) and card products, but its stated winter-single period ends 13 June 2026; the applicable 13–19 October fare is not established. One static Route 186 variant lists a 20:53 Stadium departure; run the date-specific planner in both directions and keep a live-quote taxi/ride-hailing alternative for a late finish, especially on 17 October.

records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is the only route in the operator's tables that links Qawra's seafront stops directly to the Ta' Qali stadium stop, but it is ASYMMETRIC and that is the single most important transport fact for this trip. Traced stop by stop on 11 October 2026, the direction that serves Il-Qawra (Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952) runs toward Ta' Qali and Rabat, while the return from opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 lists NO Il-Qawra stop at all and terminates at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). A return to AX ODYCY on Route 186 therefore always means alighting in the Buġibba area and boarding a second service toward Qawra, and the last listed return departure from Stadium 2194 is 20:53 — the binding constraint for a late playoff finish. One single fare covers both legs because onboard tickets are valid two hours with free transfers. These are published static departure grids for the current timetable, not a saved date-specific journey; the walk from stop 6227 or 2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate has not been measured, and the onward Buġibba → Qawra connection must come from the dated planner rather than be inferred from the operator's stop lists.

records.name: Route 186 diversion and the wider Ta’ Qali / Mosta evening detour cluster — 17–18 October, with two conflicting published windows
records.address: Route 186 toward Buġibba; affected stops listed by MPT are Gholja 2 through Targa
records.hours: Operator notices for the same diversion display two different evening windows: the Route 186 page reads weekly Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October (ending 18 October approx. 00:00), and the service-updates page read later on 11 October reads 20:00–24:00 for the same dated notice. Plan for the union, 19:00–24:00, and treat the live planner as authoritative.
records.description: Malta Public Transport carries a Route 186 detour notice for Friday/Saturday evenings starting 17 October 2026 and ending 18 October at approximately 00:00, stating that toward Buġibba the stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served. The operator publishes TWO DIFFERENT evening windows for that same dated notice, and both were read on 11 October 2026: the Route 186 page shows it as 19:00–00:00, while the latest-service-updates page showed 20:00–24:00. Plan for the UNION, 19:00–24:00, and treat the live planner as authoritative on the day. The omitted-stop notice gives no diverted path and does not say whether a particular Stadium departure, the 20:53 entry in one static variant, or an onward Qawra connection is cancelled or altered. Treat it as a potential disruption risk, not proof that the route or all bus returns are unavailable; use the dated planner to check every route and keep a live taxi/ride-hailing quote as a fallback. The same service-updates page lists a CLUSTER of further companion detours on the identical Friday/Saturday evening pattern from 17 October affecting Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 in the Mosta, Rotunda and Ta’ Qali P&R area — including Route 405 omitting Rotunda 1 and Bezzina toward Mosta/Ta’ Qali P&R and Route 47 omitting Gatt through Rotunda 1 toward Mosta — so any Mosta-changing return plan needs rechecking too. A large open-air event is ticketed at UNO Malta in Ta’ Qali, Attard from 22:00 on Saturday 17 October, which is consistent with that cluster, but MPT names no cause and none is asserted here. The page also carries a separate, longer-running weekly Friday/Saturday 20:00–00:00 detour ending 21 April with the same affected-stop wording, so the operator is publishing overlapping notices. One ambiguity is worth flagging: 17 October 2026 is a Saturday and the notice’s explicit end is 18 October at approximately 00:00 (midnight ending Saturday), yet the same sentence says the detour runs “weekly on Friday, Saturday”, so whether it also applies on Friday 16 October is not clear from the text and must be checked with the operator or the planner. Treat the notices as a reason to recheck the Ta’ Qali/Mosta options after 19:00 on 17 October; they do not establish that no bus return is available. Plan with a live route-planner check and keep a taxi or ride-hailing quote as a fallback.
records.notes: Read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ under “Latest Service Updates”: a detour weekly on Friday and Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October, ending 18 October at about 00:00, “Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served”; and a second notice weekly on Friday and Saturday 20:00–00:00 ending 21 April with identical affected-stop wording. The same page also lists a stop closure at Saqqajja (ID 4627) on Routes 109, 109A, 181, 182, 186, 201, 202, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56 and N52, ends 1 January approximately 04:00, and Tuesday 13 October 09:30–17:30 construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. All-service-updates page: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Do not infer a cancelled or extra TWC service from these notices. The notice specifies affected stops rather than a total cancellation of Route 186, and it does not itself confirm whether a particular post-event bus will serve the required Qawra stop. Also listed on the operator’s service-updates page on 11 October 2026: Tuesday 13 October (09:30–17:30) construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. Recheck the operator’s updates and planner on the day. Third-pass addition (11 October 2026), read on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ : the wider Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 cluster from 17 October covers Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 around Mosta, Rotunda and Ta' Qali P&R. MPT states no cause for the cluster; the UNO Malta event is recorded separately in data/activities.json from the official ticketing platform and is NOT presented as the operator's stated reason. The Route 186 notice wording is: "Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served." Independently re-read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . The live notice reads: “Buses on Route 186 will be on detour. Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served.” Ambiguity to note: 17 October 2026 is a Saturday and the explicit end time is 18 October at approximately 12:00 AM (that is, midnight ending Saturday 17 October), yet the same sentence says the detour runs “weekly on Friday, Saturday”. Whether it also applies on Friday 16 October is therefore not clear from the text and must be checked with the operator or the planner. The notice also describes the Buġibba-bound direction only; it does not say whether the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops used by this trip are affected. A parallel re-read of the same pages on 11 October 2026 independently recorded the window discrepancy described above (19:00–00:00 on the Route 186 page against 20:00–24:00 on the service-updates page for the same dated notice) and judged the companion Mosta/Rotunda cluster to run 19:00–24:00; that reading is folded in here rather than kept as a second record. Neither reading resolves which window the operator will actually apply, so the union is used and the live planner remains authoritative.

At the time of checking no timetable was published for TQ1 and no TWC-specific notice was found, so this must be treated as a possibility to monitor, not a plan to rely on. records.name: Official white-taxi meter tariff — the legal maximum you can be charged
records.area: Malta (250 licensed taxis; Gozo taxis may only drive in Malta for airport or hospital trips)
records.address: Not applicable — regulated fare structure published by Transport Malta
records.hours: Taxis may be hailed where it is safe to stop, taken from designated taxi stands, booked from taxi booths, booked through the Taxi App, or pre-booked by phone, email or internet.
records.price range: Published maximum metered tariff: initial €3.50; first 1 km €2.50/km; 1–5 km €1.60/km; 5–10 km €1.40/km; 10–15 km €1.30/km; 15–20 km €1.00/km; 20 km onwards €0.85/km. Drivers may charge less.
records.description: Because the event return will almost certainly be a taxi, it is worth knowing the regulated ceiling. Transport Malta publishes these as maximum fares for a metered trip hired where there is no authorised taxi booth, and explicitly allows drivers to discount them. Worked arithmetic at the published maxima, excluding any waiting or traffic charge: 5 km caps at €12.40, 10 km at €19.40, 15 km at €25.90 and 20 km at €30.90. Those figures are this guide's arithmetic from the published bands, not quotes, and the road distance from Qawra to the Ta' Qali venue was not measured. Two extras to note: a flat €4.50 is added on 25 December and 1 January only, which does not affect this trip; and fares rise by 50% only for a taxi legally carrying more than six people with more than five passengers aboard.
records.notes: Read directly from Transport Malta's taxi page on 11 Oct 2026. Taxi services are regulated under the Taxi Services Regulations S.L.499.59: https://legislation.mt/eli/sl/499.59/eng/pdf . IMPORTANT CURRENCY CAVEAT: the page footer states 'Page last updated: 06/04/2022', so these maxima have not been re-published since April 2022 and may have been revised — confirm the current tariff or the prepaid booth price before travelling. The worked caps (€12.40 at 5 km, €19.40 at 10 km, €25.90 at 15 km, €30.90 at 20 km) are arithmetic from the published bands assuming each band is charged for its full distance, and exclude waiting and traffic charges. Separately, authorised taxi booths sell prepaid fixed-fare journeys instead of using the meter; the booth fare list was not read on the page checked. Ride-hailing apps price dynamically and are not bound by this meter tariff — compare a live app quote against the metered cap.
